correctness.rationale: Strict local best responses are exactly parity equations. The explicit two-bit recurrence z_{i+1}=z_{i-1}+(1+u_i)(1,1) has u_{i+1}=u_{i-1} and z_{i+4}=z_i, rigorously exhausting all infinitely many rung lengths through sixteen initial pairs. Separate open, straight-periodic and swap-periodic boundary counts yield respectively 1/2/1/4, 16/2/4/2 and 4/2/8/2, including all endpoint constraints. The standalone checker independently builds and tests literal adjacency best responses through n=8 and recurrence through n=100; the infinite proof does not rely on sample bounds.

originality.rationale: The standard parity-to-linear-equation reduction is explicitly known from Gilboa--Nisan and cited by Klimm--Stahlberg, and is not claimed as original. Original content is a closed mod-four enumeration and universal four-periodicity for open, cylindrical, and Möbius ladders. Sánchez Muñoz--Mc Gettrick count Nash profiles on ladders for a different anti-coordination game; their statements neither imply nor tabulate parity-response counts. No matching full family-level result was found in compared sources or accessible indexed findings; residual literature risk remains.
residual_risks: The all-graph GF(2) reduction is known; some may regard the individual ladder nullity computations as an immediate but unstated corollary. The nontrivial content asserted is the explicit, uniform three-topology enumeration and its four-periodic structure.
An equivalent mod-four ladder census in unindexed combinatorics or game-theory literature cannot be excluded.
The conclusion does not generalize to degree-four vertices under the finite support response rule T(k)=1 iff k in {0,2}.

value.rationale: A natural complete equilibrium classification for three infinite canonical ladder topologies, with all profiles represented by universal four-periodic patterns. The uniformly bounded counts despite 2n strategic players and the topology-sensitive differences contrast sharply with exponential counts from a distinct but widely studied pairwise anti-coordination game on the same graph geometries, revealing a meaningful consequence of the public-goods response structure.
